text:
Gabe Perreault, the Rangers' 23rd overall pick in 2023, is 21 and in the top six, and The New York Times has written about his calm approach to getting better: "There's still more there." Seven goals and 11 points in 21 games is a solid first full season so far, and he's scored in three of his last five.

The finishing is fair, 7 goals on 6.1 expected, and his own chances, about 1.05 expected goals per 60, are in line with what he showed last season. Our model's closest comparison is Igor Chernyshov in San Jose, another young winger who gets to dangerous spots. The Rangers take 53% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, about their team level, though the shot-attempt share (44%) shows they spend real time defending with him out there.

History is kind to players drafted where he was: of the 111 forwards picked 18th to 28th from 2005 on with four or more seasons, 64 reached 200 NHL games, and the median first full season was 0.37 points a game. He's at 0.52. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, in a small sample, had 60% of his shots coming off the rush. Our talent range projects about 22 goals.
